title: Stage dispatch and settlement
summary: A run settles its own target after required delivery and gates pass. A member still owing another named target's post-deploy QA or manual acceptance stays open, with no fabricated pass or waiver. Refusals name the item, requirement, phase, target and recovery. Lost responses remain unknown: read the exact preparation receipt or existing provider attempt before retrying or failing; pending attempts are preserved. A lost scoped-QA dispatch answer leaves the run in its QA stage and executing, so live QA keeps writing and the next re-drive continues. A failed stage records run status before the stage; a refused status write reports run_failure_unrecorded and changes neither. Fleet preparation exposes current subphases, pending heartbeats, elapsed time and reader counts in the existing driver capture. Copy-scoped batches preserve every canonical reader check and physical connection closure. When a bounded scoped-QA wait ends with blockers, the driver retains the awaiting-QA outcome even if the subsequent diagnostic report read fails. It labels fresh details unavailable and preserves the last known blocker diagnostic without fresh counts, success or gate waiver. Member settlement credits exact member-bound checks and shared plan copies owned by that member, using the done gate ownership rule. Pending or failing owned copies still block; unrelated shared groups do not count. A member removed while dispatch prepares its QA refuses as deployment_member_removed under the run lock, and dispatch skips it. A dispatch whose database lock wait is cancelled or times out answers qa_stage_dispatch_interrupted with the SQLSTATE and lock holder as a held QA wait: the run stays executing at the stage and the driver re-dispatches it. The gate holds the run lock only for each acceptance write and commits it, so a dispatch walk never carries the lock into the next member.
